_note: THE RECEIPT for pricing.yaml: the vendor's own pricing object for every model
the eval battery prices, AND for every endpoint that serves it, copied verbatim
on the date recorded beside it. Rates are USD PER TOKEN here, as the vendor
publishes them; pricing.yaml records them per MILLION, and that scaling is the
only transformation applied to the model-level block.
It exists because every error found so far was a TRANSCRIPTION or SCOPE error,
not a judgement one, and none of them was visible by reading the file:
round 1  the capture recipe dropped .pricing.overrides, so eleven models lost
every tier they are billed at.
round 2  .pricing was treated as THE price. It is one endpoint's price, and
15 of these 20 models are served by 5 to 34 endpoints spanning up to
22x. The endpoints array below is what makes that checkable.
round 3  `cheapest` in pricing.yaml was derived from an endpoint's POSITION in
that array, on the claim this note used to make: that the vendor
returns them cheapest first. It does not.
captured_on, source, endpoint and routing in pricing.yaml are a CLAIM; this file
is the evidence for it, and TestShippedPricesMatchTheCapturedVendorResponse
re-derives one from the other on every `go test` and fails on drift in either
direction — including the routing minima and maxima, which are derived from the
endpoints array here rather than typed.
Provenance is per model because rates are refreshed one model at a time. To
refresh one, replace its block here and its entry in pricing.yaml together:
curl -s https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models |
jq '.data[] | select(.id == "MODEL/ID") | .pricing'
curl -s https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/MODEL/ID/endpoints |
jq '[.data.endpoints[] | {tag, provider_name, pricing}]'
Copy the objects WHOLE. Every key is kept, including the ones pricing.yaml does
not bill (web_search, image, audio, input_cache_write_1h, internal_reasoning,
discount): the decoder rejects a key it has not seen before, so a new billable
dimension arrives as a test failure at the moment of capture instead of as
silence.
THE ENDPOINTS ARRAY IS NOT SORTED BY PRICE and its order carries no pricing
meaning at all — it is unsorted for 8 of the 20 models, in every case because a
half-price `/flex` service tier is listed after the standard one. Reading
`cheapest` off it named, for those eight, an endpoint costing exactly 2.00x the
band floor recorded beside it, and never one below. Derive `cheapest` and
`dearest` from the rates:
jq -r '.data.endpoints | sort_by(.pricing.prompt|tonumber) |
(first|"cheapest \(.tag)"), (last|"dearest \(.tag)")'
Ties at either extreme are normal — six of claude-opus-5's seven endpoints share
its floor — so any endpoint AT the extreme is a correct label. One merely near it
is not.
